channel.title: Hartford Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hartford Business Journal (hartfordbusiness.com)

item.title: West Hartford approves 54-unit affordable housing development
item.description: A proposal to build six two-story buildings with a total of 54 affordable multifamily residential units in West Hartford was unanimously approved Tuesday night by the Town Council.

item.title: CT industrial magnet producer acquired
item.description: A Shelton-based manufacturer of magnetic components and transformer products has been sold to an individual buyer.

item.title: 🔒 Site at Waterbury-Middlebury line eyed for apartments or hotel
item.description: Site at Waterbury-Middlebury line eyed for apartments or hotel

item.title: 🔒 Breeze Airways adds Louisville route at Bradley International Airport
item.description: Budget airline Breeze Airways will launch nonstop service this summer between Bradley International Airport and Louisville, Kentucky, the Connecticut Airport Authority announced Wednesday.

item.title: 🔒 Amphenol posts record results, discloses up to $300M potential China tax exposure
item.description: The electronics and fiber-optic connector manufacturer said fourth-quarter sales rose 49% from a year earlier to $6.44 billion.

item.title: 🔒 Groton’s Electric Boat fuels revenue surge at General Dynamics
item.description: Marine systems’ revenue was up 22% in the fourth quarter, something that CEO Phebe Novakovic called a “remarkable growth story.”

item.title: PE-backed CT masonry business acquires New England manufacturer
item.description: US Masonry and Building Products said it purchased York Flashings LLC, which manufactures products designed to seal joints and channel moisture out of building walls to help prevent water damage.

item.title: 🔒 Following Halda Therapeutics deal, CI banks $41M in 2Q venture proceeds
item.description: Connecticut Innovations (CI), the state’s quasi-public venture capital arm, said Wednesday it generated about $41 million in returns during the second quarter of its fiscal year, which ended Dec. 31 — a sharp increase from $7 million in the first quarter.

item.title: Hartford HealthCare cancer program earns new designation in MSK partnership
item.description: Hartford HealthCare’s Cancer Institute has been designated an “MSK Care Partner” by Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, a move the organizations say formalizes clinical standards already in place through a long-running affiliation.

item.title: Update of Hartford’s underground loop heating system on hold
item.description: A contentious plan to heat state office buildings in downtown Hartford with a new generation of gas-powered boilers is on hold due to potential interference from the planned reconstruction of Interstate 84, officials confirmed this week.
